title: Pharos: Learning to Control Rare Events at Scale
abstract: arXiv:2611.26765v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Rare events drive transformations across physics, chemistry and biology, yet predicting their mechanisms and rates remains a fundamental challenge. Here we introduce Pharos, a framework that learns to make rare transitions accessible while predicting how frequently they occur under physical dynamics. Through stochastic optimal control, Pharos jointly learns the probability of completing a transition and how to steer simulations toward it, allowing sampling and learning to improve one another. Across biomolecular benchmarks, Pharos learns accurate transition probabilities with order-of-magnitude gains in convergence speed over previous algorithms. It transfers across ion assembly systems in explicit solvent while maintaining accurate reaction rate predictions, scales to host-guest binding systems that span millisecond timescales, and enables chemical reaction studies with a computationally demanding machine learning interatomic potentia

translated_title: Pharos：学习大规模控制稀有事件
translated_abstract: 稀有事件驱动着物理学、化学和生物学中的各种转变，然而预测其机制和速率仍然是一项根本性的挑战。本文提出Pharos，一个学习使稀有转变变得可及、同时预测其在物理动力学下发生频率的框架。通过随机最优控制，Pharos联合学习完成转变的概率以及如何引导模拟朝向该转变，使采样与学习能够相互促进。在多个生物分子基准测试中，Pharos学习到了准确的转变概率，收敛速度比以往算法快几个数量级。它能够在显式溶剂的离子组装系统之间迁移并保持准确的反应速率预测，可扩展到跨越毫秒时间尺度的主客体结合系统，并能借助计算开销较大的机器学习原子间势开展化学反应研究。
tldr: Pharos是一个基于随机最优控制的框架，通过联合学习转变概率与模拟引导策略使采样和学习相互促进，实现了比以往算法快数量级的收敛速度，并能扩展到毫秒时间尺度的复杂分子体系。
en_tdlr: Pharos is a stochastic optimal control framework that jointly learns transition probabilities and simulation steering strategies, allowing sampling and learning to mutually improve each other, achieving order-of-magnitude faster convergence and scaling to molecular systems spanning millisecond timescales.
